title: Max Consecutive Ones II
description:
Given a binary array nums, return the maximum number of consecutive ones if you can flip at most one zero into a one.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1,0,1,1,0]
Output: 4
Explanation: Flip the first zero to get [1,1,1,1,0]

Example 2:
Input: nums = [1,0,1,1,0,1]
Output: 4

Constraints:
- 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^5
- nums[i] is 0 or 1
idea: A window with at most one zero that never shrinks: when there are more than one zeros, the left edge moves one step together with the right edge. That is why the final window size len(nums) − l equals the best one found.
